title: Signal Across

serves.summary: The learner chooses a light or a sound signal to send a message across fog, dark, noise or a hill, which shows that people use light and sound to communicate over a distance.

request.topic: Sending a message with light or sound
request.objective: Choose a light signal or a sound signal to send a message across a distance, by what the place between sender and receiver lets through (fog, dark, daylight, noise, a hill). NGSS 1-PS4-4 (SCI001-07-d)

problems.ask: It is night. Send a message to your friend far away.
problems.goal: The lantern is on the sender: on a clear dark night a light carries far, a flag cannot be seen, and the whistle and drum are too quiet for that distance.

problems.ask: Send a message to your friend across the fog.
problems.goal: The horn is on the sender: thick fog stops even the big lamp, and sound goes through fog.

problems.ask: Send a message to your friend past the waterfall.
problems.goal: The lantern is on the sender: the loud waterfall drowns even the horn, and a light can be seen across it at night.

problems.ask: Send a message to your friend on the other side of the hill.
problems.goal: The horn is on the sender: the hill blocks every light and the flag, and a loud sound goes over the hill.

problems.ask: Send a message to both friends.
problems.goal: The horn is on the top sender (fog) and the lantern on the bottom sender (loud crowd): each path gets the signal it lets through.
